title: An exit question replayed with its amount re-rounded and its date shifted

question.text: SPY was fully exited on 2024-05-08 for about USD 30,792.00. What mainly drove that decision?

answers.note: Converted from a parallel session's finding on #417 (PR #424): a digit inside a span the engine authored is not a violation, because frozen surfaces replay verbatim and a recorded thesis may itself carry a quantity. What is a violation is quietly adjusting one — an amount rounded to a friendlier figure and a date moved to a neighbouring day both read as harmless tidying and are neither, because the user answers about the trade the stem describes.
answers.prose: SPY was closed out around 2024-05-04 for roughly USD 30,800. What mainly drove that decision?

answers.note: The frame is reworded freely; the two engine figures are carried through untouched. That combination is the whole lesson of this episode: the words are the agent's to choose, the date and the amount are not. A check that punished the quantity here would forbid faithful replay; a check that let 30,800 through would let the user answer about a trade that never happened.
answers.prose: You closed SPY out completely on 2024-05-08, taking about USD 30,792.00 off the table. Thinking back to that morning — was that an exit rule you had already set, or was it the position making you uneasy?

presented_options.label: A rule I had already set
presented_options.description: The condition I planned to exit on had been met.

presented_options.label: I wanted the gain locked
presented_options.description: It was about protecting a profit I could already see.

presented_options.label: Skip for now
presented_options.description: Leave this exit unexplained for now.
